paper_sections.title: Group differences in diffusion and kurtosis metrics derived from DKI data

description.value: A study of associations between KIBRA rs17070145 genotype, diffusion kurtosis and resting-state fMRI measures, and working-memory performance in 163 healthy young adults, including mediation analyses of left-precuneus microstructural measures.

spans.text: This study aimed to explore the effect of KIBRA polymorphism on brain microstructure and blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) fluctuations using diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in 163 young adults.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional study of healthy young adults grouped by KIBRA rs17070145 genotype.

spans.text: The study included 163 healthy, right-handed young Chinese adults (mean age: 22.9 ± 1.8 years; 53 males and 110 females).

spans.text: To investigate intragroup differences of the DKI and ALFF parametric maps, we used voxel-based independent sample t-tests in the DPABI toolbox with age, sex and years of education as nuisance covariates.

description.value: DKI maps were skull stripped, registered, normalized to MNI space, resampled to 2 mm isotropic resolution, and smoothed.

spans.text: remove the non-brain tissue from the b = 0 s/mm  image and T1-weighted image of each subject; b) register the skull-stripped T1-weighted image to the b = 0 s/mm  image for each subject using affine linear transformation; c) normalize the T1-weighted images to the Montreal Neurologic Institute (MNI) space; d) apply the transformation matrices to the corresponding diffusion and kurtosis maps and resampled to 2 mm isotropic resolution; e) smooth all images with a 6-mm full width half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel.
We used Diffusional Kurtosis Estimator (DKE version 2.0.0,   http://nitrc.org/projects/dke  ) to process the DKI data

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were motion corrected, co-registered to anatomy, normalized to MNI space, smoothed, temporally bandpass filtered, and processed to calculate ALFF.

spans.text: The detailed steps were as follows: a) discard the first 10 time points of the scan; b) correct for motion; c) co-register with high-resolution anatomical image; d) normalize to the MNI brain template (3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm); e) smooth with an 8-mm Gaussian smoothing kernel; f) perform temporal bandpass filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz).

description.value: Left precuneus cluster identified in the study's voxel-based DKI and ALFF analyses; DKI peaks included MNI coordinates approximately [-18, -34, 60 to 62], and the ALFF peak was [-15, -66, 63].

spans.text: KIBRA C-allele carriers exhibited significantly lower ALFF in the left precuneus than KIBRA TT homozygotes (x = -15, y = -66, z = 63; t = -3.58; cluster size = 92, with GRF correction, voxel   p   < 0.01, cluster   p   < 0.05) (Fig.  2 ).

description.value: Participants performed 1-back and 3-back letter working-memory conditions and responded with right or left arrow buttons.

spans.text: The task consisted of blocks of two conditions that differed in terms of working memory load (1-back and 3-back) using E-Prime 2.0 software (Psychology Software Tools, Pittsburgh, PA, USA).

description.value: Resting-state BOLD fMRI acquisition used to calculate amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation.

spans.text: ALFF was also calculated using DPABI software with the following steps: a) convert the time series of each voxel to the frequency domain using a fast Fourier transform and then obtain the power spectrum; b) compute the square root of each frequency of the power spectrum and then obtain the ALFF value; c) divide the value of ALFF of each voxel by the global mean ALFF value for standardization.
